title.zh: 卷五十一 志第四十一 食貨一
title.raw: 卷五十一 志第四十一 食貨一 Volume 51 Treatises 47: Finance and Economics 1

sentences.zh: 食貨一

translations.literal: Food and Goods, Part One
translations.idiomatic: Finance and Economics, Part One

sentences.zh: 古之善治其國而愛養斯民者，必立經常簡易之法，使上愛物以養其下，下勉力以事其上，上足而下不困。

translations.literal: Those in antiquity who governed their states well and lovingly nurtured the people always established regular and simple laws, so that those above cherished goods to nourish those below, those below strove with effort to serve those above, those above had enough and those below were not distressed.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, rulers who governed well and truly cared for their people always set up regular, straightforward laws, so that the court valued resources to support the populace, the people labored diligently to serve the throne, the state had enough, and the common folk were not ground down.

sentences.zh: 故量人之力而授之田，量地之產而取以給公上，量其入而出之以為用度之數。

translations.literal: Therefore they measured men's strength to grant them fields, measured the land's yield to take from it to supply the public above, and measured its intake to disburse it as the number for expenditures.
translations.idiomatic: They gauged each person's capacity when allotting land, gauged what the soil could produce when levying tribute for the state, and gauged revenue against outlays to set the budget.

sentences.zh: 是三者常相須以濟而不可失，失其一則不能守其二。

translations.literal: These three things constantly depended on one another to succeed and could not be lost; lose one and the other two could not be kept.
translations.idiomatic: These three measures always had to work together; lose any one of them and the other two could not hold.

sentences.zh: 及暴君庸主，縱其佚欲，而茍且之吏從之，變制合時以取寵於其上。

translations.literal: When it came to tyrannical rulers and mediocre lords who indulged their idle desires, opportunistic officials followed them, altering institutions to suit the moment in order to win favor from those above.
translations.idiomatic: But when tyrants and mediocre sovereigns indulged every whim, servile officials went along, twisting the rules to suit the moment and curry favor at court.

sentences.zh: 故用於上者無節，而取於下者無限，民竭其力而不能供，由是上愈不足而下愈困，則財利之說興，而聚斂之臣用。

translations.literal: Therefore what was used above had no restraint, while what was taken from below had no limit; the people exhausted their strength yet could not supply it. Thereupon those above grew ever more insufficient and those below ever more distressed, and then doctrines of wealth and profit arose, and ministers of aggregation and extraction were employed.
translations.idiomatic: Spending at the top knew no bounds while exactions from below knew no limit; the people gave all they had and still could not meet demand. The court grew poorer even as the masses grew poorer still, until talk of maximizing revenue flourished and extortionist ministers came to power.

sentences.zh: 《記》曰：「寧畜盜臣。

translations.literal: The 《Record》 says: "Better to keep a thieving minister."
translations.idiomatic: The 《Record of Rites》 says, "Better to harbor a thieving minister."

sentences.zh: 」盜臣誠可惡，然一人之害爾。

translations.literal: " A thieving minister is indeed detestable, yet the harm is only that of one man.
translations.idiomatic: A thieving minister is detestable, to be sure, but the harm is only that of one man.

sentences.zh: 聚斂之臣用，則經常之法壞，而下不勝其弊焉。

translations.literal: When ministers of aggregation and extraction are employed, the regular laws are ruined, and those below cannot bear their evils.
translations.idiomatic: When extortionist ministers are put in charge, the regular laws collapse, and the people cannot survive the damage.

sentences.zh: 唐之始時，授人以口分、世業田，而取之以租、庸、調之法，其用之也有節。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tang, fields were granted to people as koufen and shiye land, and taken from them by the methods of zu, yong, and diao; their use also had restraint.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the Tang, the state granted koufen and hereditary estate fields and collected revenue through the zu, yong, and diao levies, and spending was kept within bounds.

sentences.zh: 蓋其畜兵以府衛之制，故兵雖多而無所損；

translations.literal: For they kept troops by the fubing and guard system, so though the army was numerous it suffered no loss;
translations.idiomatic: Troops were maintained through the fubing militia and guard system, so a large army did not drain the treasury;

sentences.zh: 設官有常員之數，故官不濫而易祿。

translations.literal: offices were established with a fixed number of posts, so offices were not excessive and salaries were easy to provide.
translations.idiomatic: and offices had fixed quotas, so posts were not multiplied beyond need and salaries remained manageable.

sentences.zh: 雖不及三代之盛時，然亦可以為經常之法也。

translations.literal: Though it did not reach the flourishing age of the Three Dynasties, it could still serve as a regular law.
translations.idiomatic: It fell short of the golden ages of the Three Dynasties, yet it could still stand as a durable, regular system.

sentences.zh: 及其弊也，兵冗官濫，為之大蠹。

translations.literal: When its abuses came, redundant troops and excessive offices became a great bane.
translations.idiomatic: When the system decayed, bloated armies and swollen bureaucracies became its greatest curse.

sentences.zh: 自天寶以來，大盜屢起，方鎮數叛，兵革之興，累世不息，而用度之數，不能節矣。

translations.literal: From the Tianbao era onward, great bandits arose repeatedly, frontier commands rebelled again and again, the rise of arms and armor continued for generations without cease, and the figures for expenditures could no longer be restrained.
translations.idiomatic: From the Tianbao reign onward, major rebellions broke out again and again, military governors rose in repeated revolt, and warfare raged across generations without pause, until the budget could no longer be kept in check.

sentences.zh: 加以驕君昏主，奸吏邪臣，取濟一時，屢更其制，而經常之法，蕩然盡矣。

translations.literal: Added to this were arrogant rulers and benighted lords, treacherous clerks and wicked ministers, who sought temporary relief and repeatedly altered the system, until the regular laws were utterly swept away.
translations.idiomatic: Arrogant emperors and muddled sovereigns, corrupt clerks and scheming ministers, scrambling for stopgap revenue and rewriting the rules again and again, until the regular system was gone altogether.

sentences.zh: 由是財利之說興，聚斂之臣進。

translations.literal: Thereupon doctrines of wealth and profit arose, and ministers of aggregation and extraction advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Then the gospel of maximizing revenue spread, and extortionist ministers rose to power.

sentences.zh: 蓋口分、世業之田壞而為兼並，租、庸、調之法壞而為兩稅。

translations.literal: For koufen and shiye fields were ruined and became merger and absorption; the methods of zu, yong, and diao were ruined and became the two-tax system.
translations.idiomatic: Koufen and hereditary fields were swallowed up in consolidation; the zu, yong, and diao levies gave way to the two-tax system.

sentences.zh: 至於鹽鐵、轉運、屯田、和糴、鑄錢、括苗、榷利、借商、進奉、獻助，無所不為矣。

translations.literal: As for salt and iron, transport commissions, garrison farming, harmonized grain purchases, coin casting, seedling surveys, monopolized profits, merchant loans, tribute deliveries, and assistance contributions—there was nothing they did not do.
translations.idiomatic: Salt and iron monopolies, transport commissions, garrison farms, government grain purchases, coinage, seedling surveys, profit monopolies, loans to merchants, tribute deliveries, and voluntary contributions—every expedient was tried.

sentences.zh: 蓋愈煩而愈弊，以至於亡焉。

translations.literal: The more tangled it grew, the more it decayed, until the dynasty perished.
translations.idiomatic: The more elaborate the schemes grew, the worse the harm, until the dynasty itself collapsed.

sentences.zh: 唐制：度田以步，其闊一步，其長二百四十步為畝，百畝為頃。

translations.literal: Tang regulations: fields were measured by the bu; one bu in width and two hundred forty bu in length made one mu; one hundred mu made one qing.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang law, land was measured in bu: one bu wide by two hundred forty bu long constituted one mu, and one hundred mu made one qing.

sentences.zh: 凡民始生為黃，四歲為小，十六為中，二十一為丁，六十為老。

translations.literal: For the people, at first birth one was huang; at four years, xiao; at sixteen, zhong; at twenty-one, ding; at sixty, lao.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners were classified at birth as infants (huang), at four as children (xiao), at sixteen as youths (zhong), at twenty-one as adult males liable for labor (ding), and at sixty as elderly (lao).

sentences.zh: 授田之制，丁及男年十八以上者，人一頃，其八十畝為口分，二十畝為永業；

translations.literal: In the system of granting fields, for ding and males eighteen years and above, each person received one qing; of this eighty mu were koufen and twenty mu were yongye;
translations.idiomatic: Under the land-grant system, each adult male or man of eighteen and above received one qing: eighty mu as koufen (allotment land) and twenty mu as yongye (hereditary estate);

sentences.zh: 老及篤疾、廢疾者，人四十畝，寡妻妾三十畝，當戶者增二十畝，皆以二十畝為永業，其余為口分。

translations.literal: for the elderly and those with severe or crippling illness, forty mu per person; for widows and concubines, thirty mu; for household heads, an additional twenty mu—all with twenty mu as yongye and the rest as koufen.
translations.idiomatic: the elderly and the severely or permanently disabled received forty mu each; widows and concubines thirty mu; heads of household an extra twenty mu—with twenty mu always set aside as yongye and the remainder as koufen.

sentences.zh: 永業之田，樹以榆、棗、桑及所宜之木，皆有數。

translations.literal: On yongye fields, elms, jujubes, mulberries, and trees suited to the soil were planted, each in fixed numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Yongye plots had to be planted with specified numbers of elms, jujubes, mulberries, and other suitable trees.

sentences.zh: 田多可以足其人者為寬鄉，少者為狹鄉。

translations.literal: Districts where fields were plentiful enough to satisfy the people were called broad districts; where they were few, narrow districts.
translations.idiomatic: Districts with enough land to go around were termed broad districts (kuānxiāng); those with too little were narrow districts (xiáxiāng).

sentences.zh: 狹鄉授田，減寬鄉之半。

translations.literal: In narrow districts, field grants were reduced by half compared with broad districts.
translations.idiomatic: In narrow districts, allotments were cut to half the broad-district standard.

sentences.zh: 其地有薄厚，歲一易者，倍受之。

translations.literal: Where the soil was thin or thick, or the fields were rotated once a year, grants were doubled.
translations.idiomatic: Where soil was poor or fields were rotated annually, allotments were doubled.

sentences.zh: 寬鄉三易者，不倍授。

translations.literal: In broad districts with threefold rotation, grants were not doubled.
translations.idiomatic: In broad districts with three-year rotation, no doubling was granted.

sentences.zh: 工商者，寬鄉減半，狹鄉不給。

translations.literal: For artisans and merchants, in broad districts grants were halved; in narrow districts none were given.
translations.idiomatic: Artisans and merchants received half the broad-district allotment and none at all in narrow districts.

sentences.zh: 凡庶人徙鄉及貧無以葬者，得賣世業田。

translations.literal: Commoners who moved districts or were too poor to bury their dead might sell their shiye fields.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners relocating to another district, or too poor to afford burial, were permitted to sell their hereditary estate land.

sentences.zh: 自狹鄉而徙寬鄉者，得並賣口分田。

translations.literal: Those who moved from a narrow to a broad district might also sell their koufen fields.
translations.idiomatic: Those moving from a narrow to a broad district could sell their koufen land as well.

sentences.zh: 已賣者，不復授。

translations.literal: Once sold, fields were not granted again.
translations.idiomatic: Land that had been sold was never re-allotted.

sentences.zh: 死者收之，以授無田者。

translations.literal: When the holder died, the land was recovered and granted to those without fields.
translations.idiomatic: On the holder's death, the land reverted to the state and was reassigned to the landless.

sentences.zh: 凡收授皆以歲十月。

translations.literal: All recovery and granting took place in the tenth month of the year.
translations.idiomatic: All recoveries and grants were carried out in the tenth month.

sentences.zh: 授田先貧及有課役者。

translations.literal: Field grants went first to the poor and those with tax and corvée obligations.
translations.idiomatic: Land was allotted first to the poor and to households with tax and labor obligations.

sentences.zh: 凡田，鄉有余以給比鄉，縣有余以給比縣，州有余以給近州。

translations.literal: For fields in general, if a district had surplus it supplied neighboring districts; if a county had surplus, neighboring counties; if a prefecture had surplus, nearby prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Surplus land in a district went to neighboring districts; county surpluses to neighboring counties; prefectural surpluses to nearby prefectures.

sentences.zh: 凡授田者，丁歲輸粟二斛，稻三斛，謂之租。

translations.literal: For all who received fields, each ding yearly paid two hu of grain or three hu of rice—this was called zu.
translations.idiomatic: Recipients of land paid two hu of grain or three hu of rice per adult male each year—this was the land tax (zu).

sentences.zh: 丁隨鄉所出，歲輸絹二匹，綾、絁二丈，布加五之一，綿三兩，麻三斤，非蠶鄉則輸銀十四兩，謂之調。

translations.literal: Each ding, according to what his district produced, yearly paid two bolts of silk, two zhang of ling and shi, cloth with one-fifth added, three liang of cotton, three jin of hemp—or in non-sericulture districts, fourteen liang of silver—this was called diao.
translations.idiomatic: Each adult male paid yearly, according to local products, two bolts of silk, two zhang of ling and shi fabric, cloth with a one-fifth surcharge, three liang of cotton, and three jin of hemp—or, in districts without sericulture, fourteen liang of silver. This was the diao levy.

sentences.zh: 用人之力，歲二十日，閏加二日，不役者日為絹三尺，謂之庸。

translations.literal: Using men's labor, twenty days per year, with two extra days in intercalary years; those not levied for labor paid three chi of silk per day—this was called yong.
translations.idiomatic: Labor service ran twenty days a year, with two extra days in intercalary years; those exempt from corvée paid three chi of silk per day instead. This was the yong levy.

sentences.zh: 有事而加役二十五日者免調，三十日者租、調皆免。

translations.literal: When special service added twenty-five days, diao was exempted; at thirty days, both zu and diao were exempted.
translations.idiomatic: Extra service of twenty-five days exempted the diao levy; thirty days exempted both zu and diao.

sentences.zh: 通正役不過五十日。

translations.literal: Regular corvée in total did not exceed fifty days.
translations.idiomatic: Total regular corvée never exceeded fifty days.

sentences.zh: 自王公以下，皆有永業田。

translations.literal: From princes and dukes downward, all had yongye fields.
translations.idiomatic: From princes and dukes down, everyone held yongye estate land.

sentences.zh: 太皇太后、皇太后、皇后緦麻以上親，內命婦一品以上親，郡王及五品以上祖父兄弟，職事、勛官三品以上有封者若縣男父子，國子、太學、四門學生、俊士，孝子、順孫、義夫、節婦同籍者，皆免課役。

translations.literal: Relatives of the grand empress dowager, empress dowager, and empress within mourning of sizui and closer; relatives of inner consorts of first rank and above; grandfathers and brothers of commandery princes and fifth-rank officials and above; holders of fiefs among active-duty and merit officials of third rank and above, such as county marquises and their sons; students of the Directorate, Imperial University, and Four Gates, and jinshi candidates; filial sons, obedient grandsons, righteous husbands, and chaste wives registered on the same household—all were exempt from tax and corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Kin of the grand empress dowager, empress dowager, and empress within the sizui mourning circle; kin of inner consorts of first rank and above; grandfathers and brothers of commandery princes and officials of fifth rank and above; active-duty and merit officials of third rank and above who held fiefs, including county marquises and their sons; students of the Directorate, Imperial University, and Four Gates schools and jinshi candidates; and filial sons, obedient grandsons, righteous husbands, and chaste wives on the same household register—all were exempt from taxes and labor service.

sentences.zh: 凡主戶內有課口者為課戶。

translations.literal: Households with taxable persons within the chief household were called taxable households.
translations.idiomatic: Chief households containing persons liable for tax were classified as taxable households (kèhù).

sentences.zh: 若老及男廢疾、篤疾、寡妻妾、部曲、客女、奴婢及視九品以上官，不課。

translations.literal: The elderly, males with crippling or severe illness, widows and concubines, retainers, guest women, slaves, and those treated as officials of ninth rank and above were not levied.
translations.idiomatic: The elderly, men with crippling or severe illness, widows and concubines, retainers, guest women, slaves, and persons treated as officials of ninth rank and above were not taxed.

sentences.zh: 凡裏有手實，歲終具民之年與地之闊狹，為鄉帳。

translations.literal: Every li kept a shoushi register; at year's end it compiled the people's ages and the breadth and narrowness of their land into a district account.
translations.idiomatic: Each li maintained a household register (shoushi); at year's end it compiled ages and land measurements into a district roll.

sentences.zh: 鄉成於縣，縣成於州，州成於戶部。

translations.literal: District accounts were consolidated at the county, county accounts at the prefecture, prefectural accounts at the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: District rolls were consolidated at the county, county rolls at the prefecture, and prefectural rolls at the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 又有計帳，具來歲課役以報度支。

translations.literal: There was also a jizhang account listing the coming year's taxes and corvée to report to the Directorate of Expenditure.
translations.idiomatic: A planning account (jizhang) also listed the next year's taxes and labor obligations for report to the Directorate of Expenditure.

sentences.zh: 國有所須，先奏而斂。

translations.literal: When the state had needs, it reported first and then levied.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the state required revenue, it sought approval before levying.

sentences.zh: 凡稅斂之數，書於縣門、村坊，與眾知之。

translations.literal: All figures for tax levies were posted at county gates and village wards so the multitude would know.
translations.idiomatic: Tax amounts were posted at county gates and village wards for public notice.

sentences.zh: 水、旱、霜、蝗耗十四者，免其租；

translations.literal: Where flood, drought, frost, or locusts caused a loss of fourteen parts in ten, zu was exempted;
translations.idiomatic: If flood, drought, frost, or locusts destroyed fourteen-tenths of the crop, the land tax was waived;

sentences.zh: 桑麻盡者，免其調；

translations.literal: where mulberry and hemp were entirely lost, diao was exempted;
translations.idiomatic: if mulberry and hemp were entirely lost, the diao levy was waived;

sentences.zh: 田耗十之六者，免租調；

translations.literal: where fields lost six parts in ten, both zu and diao were exempted;
translations.idiomatic: if six-tenths of the fields were ruined, both zu and diao were waived;

sentences.zh: 耗七者，課、役皆免。

translations.literal: where the loss was seven parts in ten, all taxes and corvée were exempted.
translations.idiomatic: at seven-tenths loss, all taxes and labor service were waived.

sentences.zh: 凡新附之戶，春以三月免役，夏以六月免課，秋以九月課、役皆免。

translations.literal: For all newly attached households: in spring, corvée was exempted for three months; in summer, taxes for six months; in autumn, both taxes and corvée for nine months.
translations.idiomatic: Newly registered households were exempt from corvée for three months if enrolled in spring, from taxes for six months if in summer, and from both for nine months if in autumn.

sentences.zh: 徙寬鄉者，縣覆於州，出境則覆於戶部，官以閑月達之。

translations.literal: Those moving to broad districts were reviewed by the county and reported to the prefecture; if crossing a border, reviewed by the Ministry of Revenue; officials transmitted the reports in slack months.
translations.idiomatic: Those relocating to broad districts were verified by the county and reported to the prefecture; cross-prefecture moves required Ministry of Revenue approval, with reports filed in off-season months.

sentences.zh: 自畿內徙畿外，自京縣徙余縣，皆有禁。

translations.literal: Moving from within the metropolitan circuit to outside it, or from capital counties to other counties, was all restricted.
translations.idiomatic: Relocation from the metropolitan circuit to the provinces, or from capital counties to ordinary counties, was subject to restrictions.

sentences.zh: 四夷降戶，附以寬鄉，給復十年。

translations.literal: Surrendered households of the four barbarians were attached to broad districts and granted ten years of tax relief.
translations.idiomatic: Surrendered households from the frontier peoples were settled in broad districts and granted ten years of tax exemption.

sentences.zh: 奴婢縱為良人，給復三年。

translations.literal: Slaves manumitted to commoner status received three years of tax relief.
translations.idiomatic: Manumitted slaves received three years of tax exemption.

sentences.zh: 沒外蕃人，一年還者給復三年，二年者給復四年，三年者給復五年。

translations.literal: Frontier people captured abroad: those returning within one year received three years of relief; within two years, four years; within three years, five years.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier people captured overseas who returned within one year received three years' exemption; within two years, four years; within three years, five years.

sentences.zh: 浮民、部曲、客女、奴婢縱為良者附寬鄉。

translations.literal: Floating populations, retainers, guest women, and slaves manumitted to commoner status were attached to broad districts.
translations.idiomatic: Vagrants, retainers, guest women, and manumitted slaves were registered in broad districts.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，初稅草以給諸閑，而驛馬有牧田。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan era, a grass tax was first levied to supply the various stables, and relay horses had pasture fields.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan reign, a fodder tax was first imposed to supply government stables, and relay horses were given pasture land.

sentences.zh: 太宗方銳意於治，官吏考課，以鰥寡少者進考，如增戶法；

translations.literal: Taizong was then keen on governance; in officials' performance reviews, those with few widowers and orphans were advanced in rating, as with the law on increasing households;
translations.idiomatic: Taizong was then intent on good government; in performance reviews, officials were rated up for reducing the numbers of widowers and orphans, as under the household-growth statute;

sentences.zh: 失勸導者以減戶論。

translations.literal: those who failed in encouragement and guidance were judged by decreased households.
translations.idiomatic: and officials who failed to guide and encourage the people were penalized for declining household counts.

sentences.zh: 配租以斂穫早晚、險易、遠近為差。

translations.literal: Zu collection was apportioned with differences according to the earliness or lateness of harvest, difficulty or ease of terrain, and distance near or far.
translations.idiomatic: Land tax collection was scheduled according to harvest timing, terrain difficulty, and distance.

sentences.zh: 庸、調輸以八月，發以九月。

translations.literal: Yong and diao were delivered in the eighth month and dispatched in the ninth.
translations.idiomatic: Yong and diao levies were due in the eighth month and forwarded in the ninth.

sentences.zh: 同時輸者先遠民。

translations.literal: When delivery was simultaneous, distant populations went first.
translations.idiomatic: When deliveries coincided, distant districts were served first.

sentences.zh: 皆自概量。

translations.literal: All were measured by themselves.
translations.idiomatic: All goods were measured by the taxpayers themselves.

sentences.zh: 州府歲市土所出為貢，其價視絹之上下，無過五十匹。

translations.literal: Prefectures and districts yearly purchased local products as tribute; their value was gauged against the grade of silk, not exceeding fifty bolts.
translations.idiomatic: Each prefecture yearly purchased local products as tribute, valued against silk grades, not to exceed fifty bolts.

sentences.zh: 異物、滋味、口馬、鷹犬，非有詔不獻。

translations.literal: Rare objects, delicacies, horses for the mouth, hawks and dogs—without an edict they were not presented.
translations.idiomatic: Exotic goods, delicacies, riding horses, hawks, and hunting dogs were not presented without imperial command.

sentences.zh: 有加配，則以代租賦。

translations.literal: When extra allotments were made, they substituted for zu and other levies.
translations.idiomatic: Extra tribute assignments could be substituted for land tax and other levies.

sentences.zh: 其兇荒則有社倉賑給，不足則徙民就食諸州。

translations.literal: In famine and disaster there were community granaries for relief; when insufficient, the people were moved to eat in other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In famine, community granaries provided relief; when stores ran short, people were relocated to other prefectures for food.

sentences.zh: 尚書左丞戴胄建議：「自王公以下，計墾田，秋熟，所在為義倉，歲兇以給民。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director of the Secretariat Dai Zhou proposed: "From princes and dukes downward, counting reclaimed fields, when the autumn crop ripened, wherever they were, charity granaries were established; in years of disaster grain was given to the people."
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director of the Secretariat Dai Zhou proposed: "From princes and dukes down, based on reclaimed acreage, charity granaries should be set up wherever the autumn harvest came in, to feed the people in years of dearth."

sentences.zh: 」太宗善之，乃詔：「畝稅二升，粟、麥、秔、稻，隨土地所宜。

translations.literal: Taizong approved this and issued an edict: "Two sheng per mu in tax, of millet, wheat, jing, or rice, according to what the land suited."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong approved and decreed: "A levy of two sheng per mu, in millet, wheat, jing, or rice as the soil allowed."

sentences.zh: 寬鄉斂以所種，狹鄉據青苗簿而督之。

translations.literal: In broad districts collection followed what was planted; in narrow districts it was supervised according to the green-sprout register.
translations.idiomatic: In broad districts the levy followed actual planting; in narrow districts it was assessed from the green-sprout register.

sentences.zh: 田耗十四者免其半，耗十七者皆免之。

translations.literal: Where fields lost fourteen parts in ten, half was exempted; where seventeen parts in ten, all was exempted.
translations.idiomatic: A fourteen-tenths crop loss halved the levy; at seventeen-tenths, the levy was waived entirely.

sentences.zh: 商賈無田者，以其戶為九等，出粟自五石至於五斗為差。

translations.literal: Merchants without fields were ranked in nine grades by household, contributing grain in differences from five shi down to five dou.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants without land were graded in nine household ranks, contributing grain on a scale from five shi down to five dou.

sentences.zh: 下下戶及夷獠不取焉。

translations.literal: The lowest households and Yi and Liao peoples were not levied.
translations.idiomatic: The lowest-rank households and Yi and Liao peoples were exempt.

sentences.zh: 歲不登，則以賑民；

translations.literal: In years of poor harvest, grain was used to relieve the people;
translations.idiomatic: In lean years, grain was distributed in relief;

sentences.zh: 或貸為種子，則至秋而償。

translations.literal: or lent as seed, to be repaid by autumn.
translations.idiomatic: or lent as seed grain, to be repaid at harvest.

sentences.zh: 」其後洛、相、幽、徐、齊、並、秦、蒲州又置常平倉，粟藏九年，米藏五年，下濕之地，粟藏五年，米藏三年，皆著於令。

translations.literal: Thereafter Luoyang, Xiang, You, Xu, Qi, Bing, Qin, and Pu prefectures also established Ever-Normal Granaries: grain stored nine years, rice five; in low damp regions, grain five years and rice three—all written into statute.
translations.idiomatic: Later, Luoyang, Xiangzhou, Youzhou, Xuzhou, Qizhou, Bingzhou, Qinzhou, and Puzhou also set up Ever-Normal Granaries—grain stored nine years, rice five; in damp lowlands, grain five years and rice three—all codified in statute.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，戶不及三百萬，絹一匹易米一斗。

translations.literal: Early in Zhenguan, households did not reach three million; one bolt of silk exchanged for one dou of rice.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenguan era, registered households numbered fewer than three million, and one bolt of silk bought only one dou of rice.

sentences.zh: 至四年，米斗四五錢，外戶不閉者數月，馬牛被野，人行數千里不賫糧，民物蕃息，四夷降附者百二十萬人。

translations.literal: By the fourth year, a dou of rice cost four or five cash; outer gates were left unbarred for months; horses and cattle covered the wilds; travelers went thousands of li without carrying provisions; people and goods flourished; those of the four barbarians who surrendered and attached numbered 1.2 million.
translations.idiomatic: By the fourth year, a dou of rice cost four or five cash; outer gates stood unbarred for months on end; horses and cattle roamed the open country; travelers journeyed thousands of li without carrying provisions; population and wealth flourished; and 1.2 million people from the frontier peoples submitted.

sentences.zh: 是歲，天下斷獄，死罪者二十九人，號稱太平。

translations.literal: That year, cases judged throughout the realm numbered death sentences for only twenty-nine persons; it was called the Great Peace.
translations.idiomatic: That year, courts throughout the empire handed down only twenty-nine death sentences; the age was hailed as the Great Peace.

sentences.zh: 此高祖、太宗致治之大略，及其成效如此。

translations.literal: This was the great outline by which Gaozu and Taizong brought order, and its results were such as this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the broad strategy by which Gaozu and Taizong brought order to the realm, and such were its results.

sentences.zh: 高宗承之，海內艾安。

translations.literal: Gaozong inherited it, and within the seas all was tranquil and secure.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong carried on the legacy, and the realm within the seas knew peace.

sentences.zh: 太尉長孫無忌等輔政，天下未見失德。

translations.literal: Grand Mentor Zhangsun Wuji and others assisted in government; the realm saw no loss of virtue.
translations.idiomatic: With Grand Mentor Zhangsun Wuji and others guiding policy, the court showed no lapse in virtue.

sentences.zh: 數引刺史入閤，問民疾苦。

translations.literal: He repeatedly summoned prefectural governors into the palace chambers to ask about the people's hardships.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly summoned prefectural governors to the palace to inquire after the people's hardships.

sentences.zh: 即位之歲，增戶十五萬。

translations.literal: In the year of his accession, households increased by 150,000.
translations.idiomatic: In the year of his accession, registered households rose by 150,000.

sentences.zh: 及中書令李義府、侍中許敬宗既用事，役費並起。

translations.literal: When Chief Minister Li Yifu and Attendant-in-Attendance Xu Jingzong came to power, corvée and expenditures arose together.
translations.idiomatic: Once Chief Minister Li Yifu and Attendant-in-Attendance Xu Jingzong gained power, corvée and spending rose together.

sentences.zh: 永淳以後，給用益不足。

translations.literal: After the Yongchun era, supplies and expenditures grew ever more insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yongchun reign, revenue increasingly fell short of need.

sentences.zh: 加以武後之亂，紀綱大壞，民不勝其毒。

translations.literal: Added to this was the chaos of Empress Wu; regulations were greatly ruined, and the people could not bear their poison.
translations.idiomatic: Then came the turmoil of Empress Wu; institutions collapsed, and the people could not endure the oppression.

sentences.zh: 玄宗初立求治，蠲徭役者給蠲符，以流外及九品京官為蠲使，歲再遣之。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong first took the throne seeking good government, those exempted from corvée were given exemption tallies; officials outside the regular roster and capital officials of ninth rank served as exemption commissioners, dispatched twice yearly.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong first ascended the throne intent on reform, those exempted from corvée received exemption tallies; low-ranking capital officials served as exemption commissioners and were dispatched twice a year.

sentences.zh: 開元八年，頒庸調法於天下，好不過精，惡不至濫，闊者一尺八寸，長者四丈。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Kaiyuan, the yong and diao law was promulgated throughout the realm: fine grades no better than jing, coarse no worse than lan; width at most one chi eight cun, length at most four zhang.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan year 8, standards for yong and diao levies were issued empire-wide: finest grades no better than jing quality, coarsest no worse than lan; width no more than one chi eight cun, length no more than four zhang.

sentences.zh: 然是時天下戶未嘗升降。

translations.literal: Yet at this time household registers throughout the realm had never risen or fallen.
translations.idiomatic: Yet household registers empire-wide had scarcely been updated.

sentences.zh: 監察御史宇文融獻策：括籍外羨田、逃戶，自占者給復五年，每丁稅錢千五百，以攝御史分行括實。

translations.literal: Investigating Censor Yuwen Rong submitted a plan: to survey extra fields outside the registers and escaped households; those who reported themselves received five years of tax relief; each ding paid 1,500 cash in tax; acting censors were sent out by circuit to survey and verify.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating Censor Yuwen Rong proposed surveying unregistered surplus land and hidden households: self-reporters received five years' tax exemption; each adult male paid 1,500 cash; and acting censors were dispatched by circuit to verify the rolls.

sentences.zh: 陽翟尉皇甫憬上書言其不可。

translations.literal: Assistant Magistrate of Yangdi Huangfu Jing memorialized that this could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Magistrate of Yangdi Huangfu Jing submitted a memorial arguing the plan was unworkable.

sentences.zh: 玄宗方任用融，乃貶憬為盈川尉。

translations.literal: Xuanzong was then employing Rong and demoted Jing to Assistant Magistrate of Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong, then favoring Rong, demoted Jing to assistant magistrate of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 諸道所括得客戶八十余萬，田亦稱是。

translations.literal: The circuits surveyed obtained more than 800,000 client households, and fields in a like amount.
translations.idiomatic: The circuits registered more than 800,000 client households and a corresponding acreage of land.

sentences.zh: 州縣希旨張虛數，以正田為羨，編戶為客，歲終，籍錢數百萬緡。

translations.literal: Prefectures and counties, eager to please, inflated false figures, treating regular fields as surplus and registered households as client households; at year's end they registered several million strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures and counties, eager to please their superiors, inflated the rolls—reclassifying regular fields as surplus land and registered households as client households—and by year's end had logged several million strings in revenue.

sentences.zh: 十六年，乃詔每三歲以九等定籍。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, an edict was issued that every three years the registers should be fixed by nine grades.
translations.idiomatic: In year 16, an edict ordered household registers to be reassessed on a nine-grade scale every three years.

sentences.zh: 而庸調折租所取華好，州縣長宮勸織，中書門下察濫惡以貶官吏，精者褒賞之。

translations.literal: The yong, diao, and cloth-for-rent levies were to take only fine and good goods; prefectural and county chiefs urged weaving; the Secretariat and Chancellery inspected for coarse and inferior goods to demote officials, and rewarded the finest.
translations.idiomatic: Yong, diao, and grain-for-rent payments were required in the finest quality; local magistrates urged weaving; the Secretariat inspected for shoddy goods and demoted negligent officials, while rewarding excellence.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，詔男十五、女十三以上得嫁娶。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, an edict allowed males of fifteen and females of thirteen and above to marry.
translations.idiomatic: In year 22, an edict permitted marriage for males aged fifteen and females aged thirteen and above.

sentences.zh: 州縣歲上戶口登耗，采訪使覆實之，刺史、縣令以為課最。

translations.literal: Prefectures and counties yearly reported household increases and decreases; investigating commissioners verified the figures; prefects and magistrates were judged on this for their performance rating.
translations.idiomatic: Each year prefectures and counties reported household growth and decline; investigating commissioners verified the figures; and prefects and magistrates were rated on the results.

sentences.zh: 初，永徽中禁買賣世業、口分田。

translations.literal: At first, in the Yonghui era, the sale of shiye and koufen fields was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yonghui reign, the sale of hereditary estate and koufen land was prohibited.

sentences.zh: 其後豪富兼並，貧者失業，於是詔買者還地而罰之。

translations.literal: Thereafter the wealthy and powerful merged and absorbed land, the poor lost their livelihoods, and so an edict ordered buyers to return the land and be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as the rich consolidated holdings and the poor lost their livelihoods, an edict required buyers to return the land and face penalties.

sentences.zh: 先是楊州租、調以錢，嶺南以米，安南以絲，益州以羅、䌷、綾、絹供春彩。

translations.literal: Previously Yangzhou paid zu and diao in cash, Lingnan in rice, Annan in silk, and Yizhou supplied gauze, chou, ling, and juan for spring tribute silks.
translations.idiomatic: Previously Yangzhou paid land tax and diao in cash, Lingnan in rice, Annan in silk, and Yizhou furnished gauze, chou, ling, and silk for spring tribute fabrics.

sentences.zh: 因詔江南亦以布代租。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered Jiangnan also to substitute cloth for zu.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then extended the practice to Jiangnan, allowing cloth to substitute for the land tax.

sentences.zh: 中書令李林甫以租庸、丁防、和糴、春彩、稅草無定法，歲為旨符，遣使一告，費紙五十余萬。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Li Linfu, because zu, yong, frontier garrison, harmonized grain purchase, spring silks, and grass tax had no fixed law and yearly produced directive tallies sent by envoys in a single notice, consumed more than five hundred thousand sheets of paper.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Li Linfu noted that land tax, yong, frontier garrison duty, government grain purchases, spring silks, and fodder tax lacked fixed rules; each year produced directive tallies dispatched by envoys in a single notice, consuming more than five hundred thousand sheets of paper.

sentences.zh: 條目既多，覆問逾年，乃與采訪朝集使議革之，為長行旨，以授朝集使及送旨符使，歲有所支，進畫附驛以達，每州不過二紙。

translations.literal: The entries being numerous, replies took more than a year; he then discussed reform with investigating and assembly commissioners, making standing directives to hand to assembly commissioners and directive envoys; yearly expenditures were listed, submitted in draft and sent by post relay, with no more than two sheets per prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: With so many entries, follow-up inquiries dragged on for more than a year. He then worked with investigating and assembly commissioners to reform the system into standing directives for assembly commissioners and dispatch envoys; annual expenditures were listed, submitted in draft, and relayed by post—no more than two sheets per prefecture.

sentences.zh: 凡庸、調、租、資課，皆任土所宜，州縣長官涖定粗良，具上中下三物之樣輸京都。

translations.literal: For all yong, diao, zu, and material levies, each followed what the land suited; prefectural and county chiefs personally fixed coarse and fine grades and submitted samples of upper, middle, and lower goods to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yong, diao, land tax, and material levies all followed local products; magistrates set coarse and fine grades and sent samples of upper, middle, and lower quality to the capital.

sentences.zh: 有濫惡，督中物之直。

translations.literal: If goods were coarse and inferior, the price of middle-grade goods was exacted.
translations.idiomatic: Shoddy goods were charged at middle-grade prices.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，以江、淮輸運有河、洛之艱，而關中蠶桑少，菽粟常賤，乃命庸、調、資課皆以米，兇年樂輸布絹者亦從之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, because Jiang-Huai transport faced the hardships of the Yellow and Luo rivers, while Guanzhong had little sericulture and beans and grain were always cheap, an order made yong, diao, and material levies all payable in rice; in famine years those willing to pay in cloth and silk were also allowed.
translations.idiomatic: In year 25, because transport from the Jiang-Huai region faced the obstacles of the Yellow and Luo rivers, while Guanzhong produced little silk and grain prices were chronically low, yong, diao, and material levies were ordered payable in rice; in famine years cloth and silk payments were also accepted.

sentences.zh: 河南、北不通運州，租皆為絹，代關中庸、課，詔度支減轉運。

translations.literal: In Henan north and south, prefectures without transport links paid zu entirely in silk, substituting for Guanzhong yong and levies; the Directorate of Expenditure was ordered to reduce transport.
translations.idiomatic: In north and south Henan, prefectures without transport links paid the land tax entirely in silk, substituting for Guanzhong yong and levies, and the Directorate of Expenditure was ordered to cut transport costs.

sentences.zh: 明年，又詔民三歲以下為黃，十五以下為小，二十以下為中。

translations.literal: The next year, another edict made those under three years huang, under fifteen xiao, and under twenty zhong.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, another edict classified those under three as infants, under fifteen as children, and under twenty as youths.

sentences.zh: 又以民間戶高丁多者，率與父母別籍異居，以避征戍，乃詔十丁以上免二丁，五丁以上免一丁，侍丁孝者免徭役。

translations.literal: Also, because among the people households with high rank and many adult males commonly separated registers and lived apart from parents to avoid levy and garrison duty, an edict exempted two ding from households of ten or more and one ding from five or more; filial sons serving parents were exempt from corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Because wealthy households with many adult sons commonly split registers and lived apart from parents to evade taxes and garrison duty, an edict exempted two adult males from households of ten or more and one from households of five or more, and filial sons caring for parents were exempt from corvée.

sentences.zh: 天寶三載，更民十八以上為中男，二十三以上成丁。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianbao, males eighteen and above were made zhongnan, and twenty-three and above became ding.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao year 3, males eighteen and above were classified as zhongnan, and those twenty-three and above as full adult males liable for labor.

sentences.zh: 五載，詔貧不能自濟者，每鄉免三十丁租庸。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, an edict granted that those too poor to support themselves would have thirty ding per district exempted from zu and yong.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5, an edict exempted thirty adult males per district from land tax and yong for households too poor to support themselves.

sentences.zh: 男子七十五以上、婦人七十以上，中男一人為侍；

translations.literal: For men seventy-five and above and women seventy and above, one zhongnan served them;
translations.idiomatic: For men aged seventy-five and above and women aged seventy and above, one zhongnan was assigned as attendant;

sentences.zh: 八十以上以令式從事。

translations.literal: for those eighty and above, regulations and forms were followed.
translations.idiomatic: for those eighty and above, the matter followed statutory regulations.

sentences.zh: 是時，海內富實，米鬥之價錢十三，青、齊間鬥才三錢，絹一匹錢二百。

translations.literal: At this time, within the seas all was rich and solid; a dou of rice cost thirteen cash; between Qing and Qi a dou was only three cash; one bolt of silk two hundred cash.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the realm was prosperous: a dou of rice cost thirteen cash; in Qing and Qi only three; a bolt of silk two hundred.

sentences.zh: 道路列肆，具酒食以待行人，店有驛驢，行千里不持尺兵。

translations.literal: Shops lined the roads, providing food and drink for travelers; relay stations had post mules; one traveled a thousand li without carrying a foot of arms.
translations.idiomatic: Shops lined the highways offering food and drink to travelers; relay stations kept post mules; one could travel a thousand li without carrying weapons.

sentences.zh: 天下歲入之物，租錢二百余萬緡，粟千九百八十余萬斛，庸、調絹七百四十萬匹，綿百八十余萬屯，布千三十五萬余端。

translations.literal: The realm's yearly intake was: zu in cash more than two million strings; grain more than 19.8 million hu; yong and diao silk 7.4 million bolts; cotton more than 1.8 million tun; cloth more than 10.35 million duan.
translations.idiomatic: Annual revenue empire-wide amounted to more than two million strings in land tax cash, 19.8 million hu of grain, 7.4 million bolts of yong and diao silk, 1.8 million tun of cotton, and 10.35 million duan of cloth.

sentences.zh: 天子驕於佚樂而用不知節，大抵用物之數，常過其所入。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven grew arrogant in idle pleasure and did not know restraint in spending; generally the figures for what was used constantly exceeded what came in.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew arrogant in pleasure and knew no restraint in spending; expenditures routinely exceeded revenue.

sentences.zh: 於是錢谷之臣，始事朘刻。

translations.literal: Thereupon ministers of cash and grain began to practice squeezing and scraping.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers of finance then turned to squeezing and scraping.

sentences.zh: 太府卿楊崇禮句剝分銖，有欠折漬損者，州縣督送，歷年不止。

translations.literal: Grand Steward Yang Chongli parsed and stripped to the fen and zhu; where there were shortages, damage, or spoilage, prefectures and counties were compelled to deliver, year after year without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Steward Yang Chongli parsed accounts to the last fen and zhu; any shortage, damage, or spoilage was pursued by prefectures and counties year after year without end.

sentences.zh: 其子慎矜專知太府，次子慎名知京倉，亦以苛刻結主恩。

translations.literal: His son Shenjin exclusively managed the Grand Steward's office; his second son Shenming managed the capital granaries; both also won the ruler's favor through harshness.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shenjin took charge of the Grand Steward's office; his second son Shenming managed the capital granaries; both curried imperial favor through harsh exaction.

sentences.zh: 王鉷為戶口色役使，歲進錢百億萬緡，非租庸正額者，積百寶大盈庫，以供天子燕私。

translations.literal: Wang Hong served as commissioner for household registers and corvée levies, yearly presenting ten billion strings of cash; amounts outside the regular zu and yong quotas were piled in the Great Abundance Treasury of a hundred treasures to supply the Son of Heaven's private banquets.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hong served as commissioner for household registers and corvée levies, reporting ten billion strings of cash yearly; revenue outside regular land tax and yong quotas went to the Great Abundance Treasury to fund the emperor's private entertainments.

sentences.zh: 及安祿山反，司空楊國忠以為正庫物不可以給士，遣侍御史崔眾至太原納錢度僧尼道士，旬日得百萬緡而已。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, Minister of Works Yang Guozhong held that goods in the regular treasuries could not supply the troops; he sent Attending Censor Cui Zhong to Taiyuan to collect cash for licensing Buddhist and Taoist clergy; in ten days only one million strings were obtained.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled, Minister of Works Yang Guozhong argued that regular treasury goods could not supply the army; he sent Attending Censor Cui Zhong to Taiyuan to sell ordination licenses to monks and Taoist priests, raising only one million strings in ten days.

sentences.zh: 自兩京陷沒，民物耗弊，天下蕭然。

translations.literal: From the fall of the two capitals, people and goods were exhausted and ruined; the realm was desolate.
translations.idiomatic: After the two capitals fell, people and goods were devastated and the realm lay in ruin.

sentences.zh: 肅宗即位，遣御史鄭叔清等籍江淮、蜀漢富商右族訾畜，十收其二，謂之率貸。

translations.literal: When Suzong took the throne, he dispatched Censor Zheng Shuqing and others to register the assets of wealthy merchants and powerful families in Jiang-Huai and Shu-Han; two parts in ten were taken—this was called the proportional levy.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong ascended the throne, he sent Censor Zheng Shuqing and others to register the wealth of great merchants and powerful families in Jiang-Huai and Shu-Han, levying two-tenths of declared assets—a tax called the proportional levy.

sentences.zh: 諸道亦稅商賈以贍軍，錢一千者有稅。

translations.literal: The circuits also taxed merchants to support the army; any sum of a thousand cash was taxed.
translations.idiomatic: Circuits also taxed merchants to support the armies; any transaction of a thousand cash was taxed.

sentences.zh: 於是北海郡錄事參軍第五琦以錢谷得見，請於江淮置租庸使，吳鹽、蜀麻、銅冶皆有稅，市輕貨繇江陵、襄陽、上津路轉至鳳翔。

translations.literal: Thereupon Di Wuqi, Lu Shi Canjun of Beihai Commandery, gained an audience through finance and grain matters; he requested establishing zu-yong commissioners in Jiang-Huai; Wu salt, Shu hemp, and copper smelting were all taxed; light goods were purchased and sent by Jiangling, Xiangyang, and Shangjin routes to Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Then Di Wuqi, recording officer of Beihai Commandery, gained an audience on fiscal matters and proposed zu-yong commissioners for Jiang-Huai; taxes were imposed on Wu salt, Shu hemp, and copper smelting; light goods were purchased and routed through Jiangling, Xiangyang, and Shangjin to Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 明年，鄭叔清與宰相裴冕建議，以天下用度不充，諸道得召人納錢，給空名告身，授官勛邑號；

translations.literal: The next year, Zheng Shuqing and Chancellor Pei Mian proposed that because expenditures throughout the realm were insufficient, each circuit might summon people to pay cash and receive blank commission documents, granting offices, merit titles, and fief designations;
translations.idiomatic: The next year, Zheng Shuqing and Chancellor Pei Mian proposed that, with revenue insufficient empire-wide, circuits might sell blank commission documents for cash, granting offices, merit titles, and fief designations;

sentences.zh: 度道士僧尼不可勝計；

translations.literal: ordaining Taoist and Buddhist clergy beyond counting;
translations.idiomatic: ordaining Taoist priests and Buddhist nuns beyond counting;

sentences.zh: 納錢百千，賜明經出身；

translations.literal: those paying a hundred or a thousand in cash were granted mingjing examination status;
translations.idiomatic: those paying one hundred or one thousand strings received mingjing examination credentials;

sentences.zh: 商賈助軍者，給復。

translations.literal: merchants who aided the army received tax relief.
translations.idiomatic: merchants who contributed to the armies received tax exemptions.

sentences.zh: 及兩京平，又於關輔諸州，納錢度道士僧尼萬人。

translations.literal: When the two capitals were pacified, another ten thousand Taoist and Buddhist clergy were licensed in the Guanfu prefectures by paying cash.
translations.idiomatic: After the two capitals were recovered, another ten thousand ordination licenses for Taoist priests and Buddhist nuns were sold in the Guanfu prefectures.

sentences.zh: 而百姓殘於兵盜，米鬥至錢七千，鬻籺為糧，民行乞食者屬路。

translations.literal: Yet the common people were ravaged by soldiers and bandits; a dou of rice reached seven thousand cash; they sold bran cakes for grain; beggars filled the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the people were ravaged by war and banditry; a dou of rice cost seven thousand cash; bran cakes were sold for food; and beggars lined the roads.

sentences.zh: 乃詔能賑貧乏者，寵以爵衤失。

translations.literal: An edict was then issued that those who could relieve the poor and destitute would be honored with noble rank and robes.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then honored those who could relieve the poor and destitute with noble rank and official robes.

sentences.zh: 故事，天下財賦歸左藏，而太府以時上其數，尚書比部覆其出入。

translations.literal: By precedent, the realm's wealth and levies went to the Left Treasury; the Grand Steward timely reported the figures; the Secretariat's Comparison Department reviewed receipts and disbursements.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, imperial revenue went to the Left Treasury; the Grand Steward reported figures on schedule; and the Secretariat's Comparison Department audited receipts and disbursements.

sentences.zh: 是時，京師豪將假取不能禁，第五琦為度支鹽鐵使，請皆歸大盈庫，供天子給賜，主以中官。

translations.literal: At this time, powerful generals in the capital borrowed from the treasuries without restraint; Di Wuqi, as commissioner of expenditure and salt and iron, requested that all go to the Great Abundance Treasury to supply the Son of Heaven's gifts, managed by palace eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful generals in the capital borrowed from the treasuries without restraint; Di Wuqi, as expenditure and salt-and-iron commissioner, proposed routing all revenue to the Great Abundance Treasury for imperial gifts, managed by palace eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 自是天下之財為人君私藏，有司不得程其多少。

translations.literal: From this time, the wealth of the realm became the ruler's private store; the responsible offices could not measure how much there was.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, imperial wealth became the emperor's private hoard, beyond the oversight of regular officials.

sentences.zh: 廣德元年，詔一戶三丁者免一丁，凡畝稅二升，男子二十五為成丁，五十五為老，以優民。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangde, an edict exempted one ding from households of three ding; generally two sheng per mu in tax; males twenty-five became ding, fifty-five became lao, to benefit the people.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangde year 1, an edict exempted one adult male from households of three; set a general levy of two sheng per mu; made twenty-five the age of full liability and fifty-five the age of elder status, to ease the burden on the people.

sentences.zh: 而強寇未夷，民耗斂重。

translations.literal: Yet powerful bandits were not pacified, and the people were exhausted while levies were heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Yet powerful enemies remained unpacified, the people were exhausted, and levies remained heavy.

sentences.zh: 及吐蕃逼京師，近甸屯兵數萬，百官進俸錢，又率戶以給軍糧。

translations.literal: When the Tibetans pressed the capital, tens of thousands of troops were stationed in nearby districts; the hundred officials advanced salary cash; households were also levied by quota to supply army grain.
translations.idiomatic: When Tibetans threatened the capital, tens of thousands of troops were stationed in nearby districts; officials contributed salary funds; and households were levied by quota for army grain.

sentences.zh: 至大歷元年，詔流民還者，給復二年，田園盡，則授以逃田。

translations.literal: By the first year of Dali, an edict granted returning refugees two years of tax relief; where fields and gardens were entirely lost, abandoned fields were granted.
translations.idiomatic: By Dali year 1, returning refugees received two years' tax exemption; where fields were entirely lost, abandoned land was reassigned.

sentences.zh: 天下苗一畝稅錢十五，市輕貨給百官手力課。

translations.literal: Throughout the realm, fifteen cash per mu in seedling tax; light goods were purchased to supply officials' labor allowances.
translations.idiomatic: A seedling tax of fifteen cash per mu was levied empire-wide; light goods were purchased to fund officials' labor allowances.

sentences.zh: 以國用急，不及秋，方苗青即征之，號「青苗錢」又有「地頭錢」，每畝二十，通名為青苗錢。

translations.literal: Because state needs were urgent, before autumn, as soon as seedlings turned green they were levied—called "green-sprout cash"; there was also "field-head cash" of twenty per mu; both were commonly called green-sprout cash.
translations.idiomatic: With state finances urgent, collection began before autumn while seedlings were still green—called green-sprout money; a field-head levy of twenty cash per mu was also added; both were known as green-sprout money.

sentences.zh: 又詔上都秋稅分二等，上等畝稅一斗，下等六升，荒田畝稅二升。

translations.literal: Another edict divided the upper capital's autumn tax into two grades: upper fields one dou per mu, lower six sheng, wasteland two sheng per mu.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict set the capital's autumn tax in two grades: upper fields one dou per mu, lower fields six sheng, wasteland two sheng.

sentences.zh: 五年，始定法：夏，上田畝稅六升，下田畝四升；

translations.literal: In the fifth year, the law was first fixed: in summer, upper fields six sheng per mu, lower four sheng;
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 the rates were fixed: for summer harvest, upper fields six sheng per mu, lower fields four sheng;

sentences.zh: 秋，上田畝稅五升，下田畝三升；

translations.literal: in autumn, upper fields five sheng per mu, lower three sheng;
translations.idiomatic: for autumn harvest, upper fields five sheng per mu, lower fields three sheng;

sentences.zh: 荒田如故；

translations.literal: wasteland as before;
translations.idiomatic: wasteland unchanged;

sentences.zh: 青苗錢畝加一倍，而地頭錢不在焉。

translations.literal: green-sprout cash per mu was doubled, but field-head cash was not included.
translations.idiomatic: green-sprout money per mu was doubled, but the field-head levy was dropped.

sentences.zh: 初，轉運使掌外，度支使掌內。

translations.literal: At first, the transport commissioner managed the exterior and the expenditure commissioner the interior.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, the transport commissioner managed external revenue and the expenditure commissioner internal finances.

sentences.zh: 永泰二年，分天下財賦、鑄錢、常平、轉運、鹽鐵，置二使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongtai, the realm's wealth and levies, coin casting, ever-normal granaries, transport, and salt and iron were divided and two commissioners were established.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongtai year 2, imperial revenue, coinage, ever-normal granaries, transport, and salt and iron were split between two commissioners.

sentences.zh: 東都畿內、河南、淮南、江東西、湖南、荊南、山南東道，以轉運使劉晏領之；

translations.literal: The Eastern Capital metropolitan circuit, Henan, Huainan, Jiangdong east and west, Hunan, Jingnan, and Shannan east circuit were led by Transport Commissioner Liu Yan;
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Capital metropolitan circuit, Henan, Huainan, Jiangdong east and west, Hunan, Jingnan, and Shannan east circuit fell under Transport Commissioner Liu Yan;

sentences.zh: 京畿、關內、河東、劍南、山南西道，以京兆尹、判度支第五琦領之。

translations.literal: the metropolitan circuit, Guannei, Hedong, Jiannan, and Shannan west circuit were led by the Jingzhao prefect and Acting Expenditure Commissioner Di Wuqi.
translations.idiomatic: the metropolitan circuit, Guannei, Hedong, Jiannan, and Shannan west circuit under Jingzhao Prefect and Acting Expenditure Commissioner Di Wuqi.

sentences.zh: 及琦貶，以戶部侍郎、判度支韓滉與晏分治。

translations.literal: When Wuqi was demoted, Vice Minister of Revenue and Acting Expenditure Commissioner Han Huang divided governance with Yan.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuqi was demoted, Vice Minister of Revenue and Acting Expenditure Commissioner Han Huang shared jurisdiction with Yan.

sentences.zh: 時回紇有助收西京功，代宗厚遇之，與中國婚姻，歲送馬十萬匹，酬以縑帛百余萬匹。

translations.literal: At this time the Uyghurs had helped recover the western capital; Daizong treated them generously, intermarried with China, and yearly sent one hundred thousand horses, repaid with more than a million bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs had helped recover the western capital; Daizong treated them generously, arranged marriage alliances, and each year received one hundred thousand horses in exchange for more than a million bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 而中國財力屈竭，歲負馬價。

translations.literal: Yet China's financial strength was exhausted, and each year it fell short of the horse price.
translations.idiomatic: Yet China's finances were exhausted, and each year the empire fell short of the horse payments.

sentences.zh: 河、湟六鎮既陷，歲發防秋兵三萬戍京西，資糧百五十余萬緡。

translations.literal: Once the six He-Huang garrisons had fallen, thirty thousand autumn-defense troops were sent yearly to garrison western Jing, with provisions costing more than 1.5 million strings.
translations.idiomatic: After the six He-Huang garrisons fell, thirty thousand autumn-defense troops were posted yearly to western Jing at a cost of more than 1.5 million strings in provisions.

sentences.zh: 而中官魚朝恩方恃恩擅權，代宗與宰相元載日夜圖之。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the eunuch Yu Chaoen relied on favor and monopolized power; Daizong and Chancellor Yuan Zai plotted against him day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the eunuch Yu Chaoen monopolized power through imperial favor; Daizong and Chancellor Yuan Zai plotted against him day and night.

sentences.zh: 及朝恩誅，帝復與載貳，君臣猜間不協，邊計兵食，置而不議者幾十年。

translations.literal: When Chaoen was executed, the emperor again grew estranged from Zai; ruler and minister were suspicious and at odds; frontier plans for troops and grain were set aside and undiscussed for nearly ten years.
translations.idiomatic: After Chaoen was killed, the emperor again turned against Zai; ruler and minister grew mutually suspicious; and frontier plans for troops and supplies went undiscussed for nearly ten years.

sentences.zh: 而諸鎮擅地，結為表裏，日治兵繕壘，天子不能繩以法，顓留意祠禱、焚幣玉、寫浮屠書，度支稟賜僧巫，歲以鉅萬計。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the various commands seized territory and banded inside and out, daily drilling troops and repairing ramparts; the Son of Heaven could not restrain them by law, but devoted himself to temple prayers, burning jade and silk offerings, and copying Buddhist scriptures; the expenditure office granted gifts to monks and shamans by the tens of thousands yearly.
translations.idiomatic: Military governors seized territory and acted in concert, drilling troops and repairing fortifications daily; the emperor could not restrain them by law, but devoted himself to temple prayers, burning jade and silk offerings, and copying Buddhist scriptures, while the expenditure office granted monks and shamans gifts totaling tens of thousands each year.

sentences.zh: 然帝性儉約，身所禦衣，必浣染至再三，欲以先天下。

translations.literal: Yet the emperor's nature was frugal; the robes he wore were always washed and dyed again and again, wishing to take the lead for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the emperor was personally frugal, wearing his robes washed and dyed again and again, hoping to set an example for the realm.

sentences.zh: 然生日、端午，四方貢獻至數千萬者，加以恩澤，而諸道尚侈麗以自媚。

translations.literal: Yet on his birthday and the Dragon Boat Festival, tribute from the four directions reached tens of millions; added to this were grace and favors; and the circuits still valued extravagance and splendor to flatter themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Yet on his birthday and at the Dragon Boat Festival, regional tribute reached tens of millions; favors multiplied; and circuits still competed in lavish display to curry favor.

sentences.zh: 朝多留事，經歲不能遣，置客省以居，上封事不足采者、蕃夷貢獻未報及失職未敘者，食度支數千百人。

translations.literal: Court business was often held over, unable to be dispatched for a year; a Guest Reception Office was established to house them—those whose memorials were not worth adopting, whose barbarian tribute was unanswered, or who had lost office without reassignment—feeding on the expenditure office by the thousands and hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: Court business piled up, some cases undecided for a year; a Guest Reception Office housed petitioners whose memorials were rejected, foreign envoys awaiting response, and officials awaiting reassignment—thousands fed at state expense.

sentences.zh: 德宗即位，用宰相崔祐甫，拘客省者出之，食度支者遣之，歲省費萬計。

translations.literal: When Dezong took the throne, he employed Chancellor Cui Youfu, released those detained in the Guest Reception Office, dismissed those feeding on the expenditure office, and saved tens of thousands yearly.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong ascended the throne, he appointed Chancellor Cui Youfu, released those held in the Guest Reception Office, dismissed hangers-on at state expense, and saved tens of thousands each year.
